headline: Agriculture: Opting for sustainable farming
summary: A small farmer, Mohammad Siddique Channa from Balochistan’s Lasbela district, seems contented since switching to organic cotton cultivation under organic agriculture (OA) practices. He now grows cotton on 15 acres of his land, making him one of many organic-certified cotton growers in Balochistan.He explains that OA practices in cotton cultivation reduced the expenses he used to incur on farm inputs, including urea and DAP, pesticides, non-genetically modified organism (GMO) seed, and insecticides, when he was associated with conventional agriculture methods. After starting organic cotton cultivation on two acres seven to eight years ago, he increased it to 15 acres with support from the Balochistan government and textile millers, who provided seed and other inputs.“I think we can bring considerable acreage in Balochistan for vegetables, fruits and other major crops under OA. Our land is still virgin while soil in Sindh and Punjab face degradation, but we do depend mostly on rain-fed irrigation, “ he said. His friend, Munir Roonjho, in the district’s Bela taluka, shared the same story, saying organic cotton cultivation has reduced his input costs from Rs50,000 to Rs60,000 an acre, as OA does not use fertilisers, pesticides, and GMO seeds.Farm input costs have been rising rapidly. Barring large landholders, smaller farmers fall into debt, creating a vicious circle. They commonly borrow cash from private lenders in rural areas to keep their economic cycle going, then sell the harvest at a lower price to repay loans against inputs, with urea and DAP as major components.About $1.9 per kg was earned as foreign exchange, and $0.9m as carbon credits between 2016 and 2024 in the organic cotton projectThe Economic Survey of Pakistan 2025-26 puts fertiliser’s share in the cost of production of major crops at 10-15 per cent. Farmers spend Rs1.2 trillion annually to buy fertiliser. A Rs100 increase in the price of a 50kg bag adds Rs20 billion in financial burden to farmers’ pockets nationally.OA has emerged as a viable option for lessening the burden of synthetic fertiliser use worldwide, and it is being pursued as a global movement. In Pakistan, Balochistan province seems to be leading OA practices, primarily in cotton. The provincial government passed its Balochistan Organic Policy in Nov 2024 to promote OA by involving 12,000 farmers in collaboration with WWF-Pakistan under a project.OA helps achieve sustainable agricultural practices that support biodiversity, reduce reliance on fertilisers, pesticides, and imported seeds, and ensure economic growth. Under global OA practices, growers were encouraged to use natural inputs to produce nutritious organic food while protecting the environment.As Pakistan’s largest but least developed province, Balochistan accounts for 44pc of Pakistan’s landmass.“We initially started with 219 acres under a foreign-funded project in Lasbela, Sibi and Barkhan districts in 2016,” said Dr Syed Habibullah Shah, Director Balochistan Agriculture Extension and recipient of Sitara-e-Imtiaz. He deals with OA practices in specific districts of the province.In 2019, Pakistan produced its first organic cotton bale in Balochistan, a turning point that propelled the province into the global organic cotton cultivation arena. Experts like Dr Yusuf Zafar, former chairman of the Pakistan Agricultural Research Council, noted that although organic cotton holds a marginal 1.5pc share of global cotton production, demand is on an upward trajectory. The global organic cotton market was valued at approximately $3.25bn in 2026 and was projected to expand to $50.78bn by 2034. Among 28 organic cotton-producing countries, he explained, India alone accounts for a huge 51% of global organic cotton production.Organic cotton acreage in Balochistan has now reached nearly 133,257 acres across Kohlu, Barkhan, Khuzdar, and Lasbela districts. Balochistan produced the first regenerative cotton bale in 2024. Now, Washuk, Kharan, and Dera Bugti districts are being selected for organic cotton production.Different textile/ginners groups now sponsor organic farmers in organic cotton cultivation there. They provide non-GMO seed and other necessary inputs and pay a quality premium to producers, over and above the per-40 kg seed cotton price, after a duly verified process involving third-party validation by an international certification body, i.e., Control Union.“About 159,000 organic cotton bales are produced and marketed in Balochistan from an organic 89,000 acres that are globally certified in 2025. The registered organic area reached 133,257 acres. The differential certified area between 133,257 and 89,000 is undergoing the certification process,” Dr Habib said, quoting the summary of organic cotton in FY26. He claimed that since Balochistan doesn’t have many ginning units, cotton bale numbers from Balochistan were usually reflected in other provinces, including Punjab and Sindh.He explained that Rs1.21bn (as per the project’s calculations) was paid to farmers as a quality premium in cash and kind. At the same time, $1.9 per kg was earned as foreign exchange and $0.9m towards carbon credit value between 2016-2024 in the organic cotton project.Farmers are told how to collect animal dung and urine under a protocol. When it turns into compost, they apply it to the soil along with recommended tillage. This bio-fertiliser, with more nutrients, improves water-holding capacity and soil OM, according to Mashood Siddiqui, a private company official working with Balochistan farmers.Textile millers find considerable potential for domestic organic cotton production, which was 2pc-3pc of total cotton. They argued that overall cotton crop production must reach 15m bales, up from the current 7m. It could potentially take textile exports from $19bn to $35bn annually.The writer is a Dawn stafferPublished in Dawn, The Business and Finance Weekly, October 12th, 2026

Organic cotton acreage in Balochistan has now reached nearly 133,257 acres across Kohlu, Barkhan, Khuzdar, and Lasbela districts. Balochistan produced the first regenerative cotton bale in 2024. Now, Washuk, Kharan, and Dera Bugti districts are being selected for organic cotton production.

Different textile/ginners groups now sponsor organic farmers in organic cotton cultivation there. They provide non-GMO seed and other necessary inputs and pay a quality premium to producers, over and above the per-40 kg seed cotton price, after a duly verified process involving third-party validation by an international certification body, i.e., Control Union.

“About 159,000 organic cotton bales are produced and marketed in Balochistan from an organic 89,000 acres that are globally certified in 2025. The registered organic area reached 133,257 acres. The differential certified area between 133,257 and 89,000 is undergoing the certification process,” Dr Habib said, quoting the summary of organic cotton in FY26. He claimed that since Balochistan doesn’t have many ginning units, cotton bale numbers from Balochistan were usually reflected in other provinces, including Punjab and Sindh.

He explained that Rs1.21bn (as per the project’s calculations) was paid to farmers as a quality premium in cash and kind. At the same time, $1.9 per kg was earned as foreign exchange and $0.9m towards carbon credit value between 2016-2024 in the organic cotton project.

Farmers are told how to collect animal dung and urine under a protocol. When it turns into compost, they apply it to the soil along with recommended tillage. This bio-fertiliser, with more nutrients, improves water-holding capacity and soil OM, according to Mashood Siddiqui, a private company official working with Balochistan farmers.

Textile millers find considerable potential for domestic organic cotton production, which was 2pc-3pc of total cotton. They argued that overall cotton crop production must reach 15m bales, up from the current 7m. It could potentially take textile exports from $19bn to $35bn annually.

• FPCCI urges Nepra to reject inflated, disputed claims; flags previously disallowed, unverified adjustments• Demands detailed written responses, participation in public hearings• Discos claim Rs2.64tr in revenue requirements for CY2027

ISLAMABAD: The Federation of Pakistan Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FPCCI) has opposed an additional Rs268 billion burden on consumers sought by former Wapda distribution companies (Discos) through prior-year adjustments inpower tariffs.

In a comprehensive representation, the country’s top business body, representing large and small businesses, including manufacturing industries, asked the National Electric Power Regulatory Authority (Nepra) to reject the “inflated claims” previously disallowed by the regulator or disputed by third parties.

The representation follows tariff petitions filed by 10 Discos seeking adjustments to the indexation of multiyear tariffs (2025-30) for calendar year 2027 and other consumer-end tariff adjustments.

Collectively, the Discos have claimed Rs2.64 trillion in revenue requirements for CY2027 on account of distribution and supply of power.

The FPCCI said it had constituted a special Energy Advisory Committee (EAC) to review tariff filings, including claims related to working capital, power purchase prices, prior-year adjustments (PYAs) and returns on revenue base.

The committee found that Discos were seeking to pass hundreds of billions of rupees in prior-year adjustments on to consumers.

It said a substantial portion of these claims was retrospective, contested by third parties or previously disallowed by Nepra. Some claims were inconsistently calculated against the Discos’ own formulas or lacked sufficient disclosure for independent verification.

The EAC reviewed all 10 Discos’ CY2027 indexation and PYA petitions, including financial statements and annexures, on behalf of FPCCI’s constituent chambers, trade and industry associations.

According to the FPCCI, Islamabad Electric Supply Company’s (Iesco) PYA claims exceeded 212 per cent of its proposed annual margin, while Sukkur Electric’s claims amounted to 113pc of its distribution margin.

Faisalabad Electric’s PYA claims amounted to 91pc of its distribution and supply margin, followed by Multan at 68pc and Quetta at 60pc.

The corresponding shares for Lahore, Peshawar and Gujranwala electric companies stood at 41pc, 40pc and 32pc, respectively. Tribal Electric did not disclose the figures.

“These are not routine formula-based true-ups and ought not to be approved as such,” the FPCCI said.

The representation included itemised objections for each Disco and a cross-company comparison, identifying disputed amounts, grounds for objections and proposed disallowances based on petitions, financial statements and annexures published by Nepra.

The FPCCI demanded that its objections be made part of each Disco’s tariff-setting process, including public hearings, and that the companies respond in writing to specific objections before the hearings.

It also urged Nepra to reject undifferentiated lump-sum PYA claims, require component-wise substantiation and allow trade and business bodies to participate in hearings.

Faisalabad Electric has sought Rs535bn in revenue requirements for 2027, including Rs57bn in PYAs. The FPCCI called for rejecting Rs26bn in claims involving 11-year post-retirement benefits and previously disallowed supplementary charges.

Gujranwala Electric sought Rs70.4bn, including Rs17bn in PYAs linked to 19-year-old Azad Jammu and Kashmir sovereign receivables. Sukkur Electric claimed Rs68bn, including Rs36bn in PYAs.

Lahore Electric sought the highest revenue requirement, Rs759bn, including approximately Rs33bn in PYAs. The FPCCI said Rs27bn in claims were liable to be rejected because they had not been verified.

Iesco submitted the largest PYA claim of Rs158bn within its Rs525bn revenue requirement. The FPCCI said 70pc of Iesco’s PYA claims were either disputed or involved noncash items, had been filed as a lump sum and should be rejected.

Peshawar Electric sought Rs233bn in revenue requirements, including Rs35bn in PYAs. Of these, Rs33bn related to seven-year-old input tax claims that the FPCCI described as inadmissible.

KARACHI: The Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) remained volatile during the outgoing week as escalating geopolitical tensions, elevated international oil prices and rising bond yields offset optimism over Pakistan’s Staff-Level Agreement (SLA) with the International Monetary Fund (IMF).

The benchmark KSE-100 index fell 0.6 per cent week-on-week to close at 167,089 points, shedding 1,066 points, according to Arif Habib Ltd (AHL).

Market sentiment remained subdued amid attacks on key shipping routes, with Yemen’s Houthis expanding their targets to Saudi Arabia’s civilian infrastructure and energy facilities. Ukrainian drone strikes on Russian refineries and concerns over US energy supplies also kept Brent crude above $100 a barrel, according to AKD Securities Ltd.

Index loses 1,066 points in outgoing week as Brent futures remain above $100 a barrel

The SLA on the fourth review of the Extended Fund Facility (EFF) and the third review of the Resilience and Sustainability Facility (RSF) provided some support. The agreement paves the way for disbursement of $1.2 billion under the two programmes, subject to approval by the IMF Executive Board. Total disbursements under the two programmes would reach about $5.7bn.

However, concerns over the widening trade deficit, inflation and the future interest-rate trajectory continued to weigh on investors.

According to AHL, the government raised Rs381bn against a Rs350bn target in its latest Pakistan Investment Bonds (PIBs) auction. Cut-off yields rose by 26-41 basis points across three-, five- and 10-year tenors, while the two-year yield declined by 19 basis points. Bids for 15-year bonds were rejected. The yield rise fuelled expectations of a possible policy rate hike at the next monetary policy announcement.

Pakistan’s foreign exchange reserves held by the State Bank of Pakistan rose by $15m to $21.5bn as of Oct 2. The rupee appreciated marginally by 0.03pc to close at Rs277 against the dollar.

Central government debt stood at Rs82.95 trillion at the end of August, up 7.1pc year-on-year but down 0.5pc month-on-month.

Sector-wise, banks were the biggest drag on the benchmark, shedding 566 points, followed by fertiliser companies with 234 points, automobile assemblers with 97, cement companies with 75 and textile composite firms with 43 points.

Habib Bank, MCB Bank and United Bank were the largest negative contributors, collectively accounting for 388 points of the decline. Fatima Fertiliser and Fauji Fertiliser Company also weighed on the index.

Oil marketing companies led positive contributions, adding 110 points, followed by power companies with 36 points. Pakistan State Oil was the largest individual contributor, adding 113 points, while Hub Power Company, Pakistan Oilfields, Engro Holdings and Mari Energies also supported the market.

Trading activity weakened during the week. Average daily volume fell 18.6pc week-on-week to 427 million shares, while the average traded value stood at $67m, down 2pc.

In the cement sector, despatches rose 6pc year-on-year to 4.62 million tonnes in September, supported by a 7pc increase in domestic sales, while exports remained flat. In the first quarter of FY27, despatches rose 4pc to 13.14m tonnes, with local sales up 8pc despite an 11pc decline in exports.

Banking sector deposits increased 14pc year-on-year to Rs39.2tr at the end of August, AKD Securities said. Cotton arrivals rose 5pc to 3.2m bales during September.

Oil production fell 6.4pc week-on-week to 63,700 barrels per day, while gas output declined 1.4pc to 2,999 million cubic feet per day, mainly because of lower production from northern oilfields and the Mari, Sui and Sharf fields.

Petrol prices increased 2.1pc to Rs398.96 per litre, while high-speed diesel prices fell 0.9pc to Rs395.72.

Elsewhere, Sindh Engro Coal Mining Company is expanding its Thar Block-II mine to supply additional coal to Lucky Electric Power Company, potentially enabling a complete transition to local coal and reducing reliance on imports.

Looking ahead, analysts expect quarterly earnings announcements and geopolitical developments to shape market sentiment. The index was trading at a 7.5x price-to-earnings ratio, with a dividend yield of 6.7pc.

They said easing inflation, improving economic indicators and any de-escalation in the Middle East could moderate oil prices and strengthen the case for monetary easing. However, persistent geopolitical uncertainty could continue to constrain gains.

article_text:
WASHINGTON: Nearly half of the countries eligible for concessional financing from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) are either in debt distress or at high risk of it, while their interest payments have quadrupled since 2013, Transparency International (TI) says.

In a report released ahead of the IMF and World Bank Annual Meetings in Bangkok from Oct 12 to 18, the anti-corruption organisation warns that secrecy and corruption in sovereign borrowing can also leave future generations paying for loans that benefit the powerful.

The report urges governments and international lenders to make public borrowing more transparent, strengthen safeguards against corruption and give borrowing countries a greater say in decisions that shape their debt obligations.

The report highlights the growing pressure on public finances in low- and middle-income countries. According to the report, at least 8 per cent of government revenue across these economies goes toward servicing debt. In Africa, 57pc of the population lives in countries that spend more on interest payments than on health, education and climate action.

TI highlights interest payments have quadrupled since 2013

The figures underline the difficult choices governments face as they struggle to finance essential public services while meeting obligations to creditors.

But TI argues that the problem is not simply how much countries borrow. The terms under which loans are negotiated, the disclosure of financial agreements, and how borrowed money is used also determine who benefits and who ultimately bears the cost.

“Without robust safeguards and effective controls over how loans are negotiated and managed, sovereign loans are misused and embezzled, enriching public officials and their cronies at the expense of future generations,” the report says.

Opaque agreements and weak oversight can make it hard for citizens, parliaments, and independent watchdogs to determine who approved a loan, how much a country owes, and whether borrowed funds were used for their stated purposes.

TI argues that the Bangkok meetings offer an opportunity to turn concerns about debt transparency and corruption into concrete policy commitments.

The annual gatherings bring together finance ministers, central bank governors and leaders of international financial institutions, alongside business representatives and civil society organisations. The G20 finance ministers and central bank governors will also meet on Oct 15, providing governments with an opportunity to establish political priorities on debt transparency and accountability.

Transparency International identifies several steps it wants these institutions to take.

First, governments should end secrecy surrounding sovereign borrowing. It calls on G20 countries to require bilateral creditors and private lenders operating within their jurisdictions to disclose complete, transaction-level financial and non-financial information about public debt.

The G20, working with the IMF and World Bank, should also develop common standards to limit confidentiality clauses in sovereign lending agreements. Such agreements, the report argues, should be consistent with borrowers’ access-to-information rules, including requirements for proactive disclosure and the legal consequences of withholding information.

headline: KP to launch six-year fiscal reform programme
summary: ISLAMABAD: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, which remains structurally dependent on federal transfers, will launch a six-year World Bank-supported programme to strengthen its fiscal system and lay the foundation for improved service delivery.The World Bank is expected to approve a $200 million loan from the International Development Association (IDA) later this month to fund the programme’s expenditure framework for fiscal years 2027-32. The programme’s total financing is estimated at $650m, with the remaining amount to be provided by the KP government.Interventions related to taxation in the merged districts and former Provincially Administered Tribal Areas (Pata) are excluded from the Programme-for-Results (PforR) financing boundary because the provincial government has extended their tax-exempt status. The programme’s $20m investment project financing component will provide technical assistance in these areas.The primary beneficiaries of the Public Resources for Inclusive Development (PRID) Multiphase Programmatic Approach for KP are the province’s 41 million residents, who are expected to benefit from better-resourced and more efficient public services. Direct beneficiaries include recipients of improved healthcare and education services.World Bank is expected to approve $200m loan for revenue mobilisation, fiscal management and service deliveryTaxpayers and businesses, including more than 700,000 property owners, around 10,000 agricultural income taxpayers, and over one million vehicle owners, are expected to benefit from more transparent, service-oriented tax administration.In the health sector, an estimated 1.3 million people are expected to benefit from improved services at rural health centres. In education, better planning, budgeting and service delivery are expected to benefit about 3.7 million pupils enrolled in public primary schools across the province, including 2.1 million boys and 1.6 million girls.Private investors are expected to benefit from access to better statistics and improved tax administration services. More broadly, improved mobilisation of own-source revenue (OSR), stronger public financial management (PFM) and evidence-based policymaking and planning are expected to align resource allocation more closely with provincial needs, ultimately improving the quality and equity of public services and investment across KP.The province’s socio-economic outlook points to fiscal vulnerability and poor development outcomes. KP remains structurally dependent on federal transfers, while OSR finances a small and declining share of rapidly rising expenditure. Inflexible salary and pension obligations dominate spending, leaving less room for public investment.Since 2022, expenditure has risen due to higher salary and pension costs, the absorption of the merged districts, inflation, and an expanded Annual Development Programme (ADP), which also covers the salaries and allowances of contract and project staff. In fiscal year 2025, 35.3 per cent of the population lived below the national poverty line. headline: Finance minister heads to Bangkok for IMF, World Bank meetings
summary: Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb on Saturday departed for Bangkok for the annual International Monetary Fund (IMF) and World Bank Group meetings.In a statement, the finance ministry said Aurangzeb would lead Pakistan’s delegation to the World Bank Group–IMF annual meetings, scheduled to be held from Oct 12 to 18.Thailand is preparing to host the IMF-World Bank annual meetings in Bangkok, bringing together more than 15,000 participants from 191 countries, including central bank governors, economic policymakers and business leaders, for discussions on the world economy.“During the visit, the finance minister will represent Pakistan at key events of the IMF and the World Bank Group and undertake an extensive programme of over 60 high-level engagements with international financial institutions, finance ministers and policymakers, development partners, global investors, banks, credit rating agencies, think tanks and international media,” the statement said.The ministry said the visit came as Pakistan continued its transition from “macroeconomic stabilisation towards sustainable, investment and export-led growth, while advancing structural reforms and strengthening engagement with international capital markets and development partners”.The statement said Aurangzeb will hold a series of high-level engagements with the leadership of the IMF and World Bank Group, including the International Finance Corporation and the Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency, focusing on Pakistan’s macroeconomic outlook, reform progress, private sector development and future cooperation.He will also attend the IMF managing director’s meeting with finance ministers, central bank governors and heads of regional financial institutions of the Middle East, North Africa, Afghanistan and Pakistan region.He will also engage with the leadership of major multilateral and development finance institutions, including the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank, the Opec Fund for International Development, the Saudi Fund for Development, the International Islamic Trade Finance Corporation, the Japan International Cooperation Agency, the ECO Trade and Development Bank, the United Nations Economic and Social Commission for Asia and the Pacific, and the International Organisation for Migration.“On the bilateral front, Aurangzeb will hold high-level meetings with counterparts from Saudi Arabia, China, Turkiye, Iran, the United Kingdom and host country Thailand, aimed at strengthening economic, investment, trade and development cooperation. He will also engage with the US Department of the Treasury to further strengthen bilateral economic cooperation and discuss Pakistan’s reform and investment agenda,” the statement said.The ministry said Aurangzeb will also meet and participate in investment seminars, sovereign investor forums and roundtable discussions with leading international financial institutions.“These engagements will provide an opportunity to highlight Pakistan’s improving macroeconomic fundamentals, structural reform agenda, international market access and investment potential,” it said.The minister will engage with Alibaba International Digital Commerce as part of discussions on Pakistan’s digital economy, e-commerce and investment opportunities.In addition, he will participate in key multilateral forums and will also contribute to high-level policy discussions.“As part of Pakistan’s international market outreach, the finance minister will hold engagements with all three major global sovereign credit rating agencies, Fitch Ratings, Moody’s and S&P Global, and present Pakistan’s economic and reform trajectory to international investors,” the statement said, adding that he would also engage with leading international media organisations.“Across these engagements, the finance minister will highlight Pakistan’s progress in restoring macroeconomic stability, strengthening fiscal and external buffers, advancing structural reforms and returning to international capital markets, while setting out the government’s priorities for investment, exports, private sector-led growth, job creation and greater financial inclusion,” it said.Additional input from Reuters

headline: PM Shehbaz orders installation of smart scanners at airports
summary: ISLAMABAD: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Saturday ordered the installation of “smart scanners” at all international airports to facilitate travellers, according to a statement from his office.The premier issued these instructions during a meeting reviewing the customs enforcement in Islamabad, attended by Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Senator Muhammad Ishaq Dar, as well as Federal Ministers Azam Nazeer Tarar, Dr Musadik Malik, Ahad Khan Cheema and Attaullah Tarar.PM Shehbaz ordered that the scanners be immediately imported and that, once installed, baggage should be screened with the new technology as opposed to being searched manually by customs officials.According to the statement, he also issued directives for customs officials, saying that passengers must not be harassed through unnecessary questioning at airports.“The prime minister further stated that outdated procedures for screening passengers’ baggage at airports must be abandoned. Passenger convenience and comfort are the top priority, and no one will be allowed to harass passengers,” the statement read.The Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) added that an “internationally established automated system will be introduced for baggage screening” and that staff providing other services at airports would be trained in line with international standards.“Courtesy and respect for human dignity in service delivery must be key components of the training,” the statement added.Commending a new enforcement system introduced by the Customs department, the premier said the initiative deserved appreciation, crediting Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) Chairman Rashid Mahmood Langrial and his team.He stressed that every possible step must be taken to curb revenue leakage, reiterating a policy of zero tolerance against tax evasion.“Tax-paying businesses are respectable, while tax evaders will face strict action. We are custodians of the poor man’s money and will protect it at all costs,” he remarked.Reviewing the customs system, the premier was briefed on the movement of goods and monitoring at various locations nationwide, and the performance of the Customs Enforcement Force and measures to prevent the smuggling of petroleum products.“The meeting was informed that significant progress had been made in establishing and operationalising Digital Enforcement Stations under Customs Enforcement,” the PMO said, adding that the Indus Collectorate, in its first three weeks of operation, executed 80 operations and seized goods worth approximately Rs205 million.“A total of 865 personnel had been deployed, covering 26 major transit routes,” it added.With operations ongoing against smuggled textiles, vehicles, cigarettes and other goods, 280 goods valuers had been recruited and would be trained this month and in November, the statement read.“The meeting was also informed that, as a result of the FBR’s reforms to prevent smuggling, the customs enforcement system had been consolidated into a single, coordinated organisation operating nationwide,” it added.

article_text:
The government has reduced petrol and high-speed diesel prices effective October 14, 2026, citing global market developments for the change.

The government on Tuesday reduced the price of petrol by Rs2.71 to Rs392.66 per litre, while cutting the price of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Re0.03 to Rs396.82 per litre, effective for Wednesday, October 14, 2026.

The Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (OGRA) revised the ex-depot prices of petroleum products under the federal government’s petroleum pricing mechanism, according to a press release issued by the Petroleum Division.

Petrol was previously priced at Rs395.37 per litre, while HSD stood at Rs396.85 per litre.

The revised prices will remain are effective for October 14.

The Petroleum Division said the change was necessitated by global developments, including movements in Platts rates, premiums and incidentals.

On Monday, the government hadreduced the price of petrolby Rs2.93 to Rs395.37 per litre, while increasing the price of diesel (HSD) by Re0.61 to Rs396.85 per litre.

Meanwhile,oil pricesfell 2% on Tuesday a day after benchmark Brent hit an almost one-month high as traders monitored attacks on Saudi Arabia and prospects for additional diesel supply from Russia.

Brent crude futureswere down $2.02, or 1.89%, to $104.63 a barrel by 1049 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate crude futures were down $1.89, or 2.02%, at $91.85 a barrel.

Both benchmarks climbed nearly $2 a barrel in the previous session, with Brent settling at its highest since September 15

The SBP has halted sugar exports from Khyber Pakhtunkhwa mills, awaiting provincial government endorsement, while Punjab and Sindh mills can proceed with their revised export quotas.

The State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) directed commercial banks on Tuesday to put sugar exports by the mills located in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s (KP) on hold till the provincial administration endorses the overseas sales of the commodity.

In a circular titled ‘Revised Instructions - Export of 200,000 MT [Metric Ton] of Sugar’, the central bank asked commercial banks to process export transaction of the commodity by eligible sugar mills located in Punjab and Sindh after the two provincial governments endorsed the revised quotas of sugar mills located in their respective territories.

“The Government of Punjab and Government of Sindh have endorsed the revised quotas of sugar mills located in their respective provinces. The endorsement from the Government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) is still awaited. Accordingly, authorised dealers [commercial banks] may process the export transactions of eligible sugar mills of Punjab and Sindh as per their revised quotas, subject to [applicable] conditions,” according to the circular.

“The endorsement of revised quota by the Government of KP will be communicated as and when received from MNFSR [Ministry of National Food Security & Research]. Accordingly, the authorised dealers shall process export transactions of eligible sugar mills located in KP after receipt of this confirmation.”

SBP said the MNFSR on October 09, 2026 had communicated the revised province and mill-wise sugar export quotas received from Pakistan Sugar Mills Association (PSMA), along with the correction to the names of three sugar mills.

Earlier in September 2026, the Economic Coordination Committee (ECC) of the Cabinet allowed export of 200,000 MT of sugar with certain terms and conditions. The ECC’s decision has also been ratified by the Federal Cabinet.

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif briefed allied parties on constitutional measures taken in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa to address security, economic stability, and terrorism, criticizing the PTI provincial government's failures.

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Tuesday briefed a parliamentary delegation of allied political parties on the situation in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP), saying constitutional measures were taken after consultations within the federal cabinet to address security concerns and safeguard economic stability.

According to a press release issued by the Prime Minister’s Office, Shehbaz said a non-partisan technocratic advisory council had been established to assist the governor in improving law and order, strengthening the economy and eliminating terrorism in the province.

The prime minister said the conduct of the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI)-led provincial government and its failure to adopt an unequivocal stance against terrorism had posed risks to Pakistan’s growing economy.

He said the federal cabinet had decided, through mutual consultation, to take constitutional measures under Articles 232 and 234 of the Constitution.

Shehbaz alleged that the KP government had neither clearly condemned terrorism nor taken decisive action against terrorists.

He said members of the armed forces, security agencies and police had sacrificed their lives over the past several years to protect the country and maintain peace in the province.

The prime minister further criticised the PTI and its provincial government, saying that over the past 13 years they had failed to deliver adequate public welfare and ensure the safety of citizens’ lives and property.

He said the federal government had provided more than Rs800 billion to KP under the National Finance Commission (NFC) framework to support efforts to eliminate terrorism.

However, he alleged, the provincial government had failed to take effective measures to strengthen the Counter Terrorism Department (CTD) and establish Safe City projects.

The parliamentary delegation included representatives of the Balochistan Awami Party (BAP), Pakistan Muslim League-Quaid (PML-Q), Istehkam-e-Pakistan Party (IPP) and Pakistan Muslim League-Zia (PML-Z).

The delegation assured the prime minister that allied parties stood with the federal government in the current situation and praised his leadership for guiding the country through difficult circumstances.

The delegation also said KP’s residents had been deprived of development in health, education and infrastructure during the PTI’s 13-year rule. It expressed confidence that, with federal government support, the province would join the country’s broader path towards development and prosperity.

Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, Defence Minister Khawaja Asif, Law and Justice Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar, Parliamentary Affairs Minister Tariq Fazal Chaudhry, and the prime minister’s adviser on political affairs and inter-provincial coordination, Rana Sanaullah, also attended the meeting.

Pakistan's car sales surged 43% in Q1 FY2026-27, driven by an improving economy and easing inflation, despite some segment declines and market hesitation.

Car sales in Pakistan rose 43% year-on-year in the first quarter of FY2026-27, with analysts attributing the hike to an improving macroeconomic environment that boosted vehicle demand.

Car sales surged by 43% to 41,872 units, while sales of jeeps and pickups decreased by 34% to 8,608 units in July-September 2026. Sales of trucks increased by 53% to 2,516 units.

However, sales of buses went down 5% to 211 units.  Moreover, sales of farm tractors also went up by 38% to 4,109 units.

Sales of two- and three-wheelers, including motorbikes and rickshaws, increased by 28% to 553,994 units, according to Pakistan Automotive Manufacturers Association (PAMA) data released on Tuesday evening.

Car sales declined by nearly 10% from 12,126 units in September 2025 to 10,939 units in September 2026.

Speaking about automotive production and sales figures during the first quarter of FY27, PAMA director general Razi-ur-Rahman said in a statement, “This renewed sales momentum is on the back of easing of inflationary pressures and an improving macroeconomic environment. During the first quarter of FY27, the industry has experienced varying trajectories across segments.”

“While overall industry volumes are steadily recovering, there is perceptible hesitation on part of the players in the market. The Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs) as well as the buyers are hesitant to take investment decisions. The lack of clarity about the auto policy continues to dominate the market sentiment,” he said.

headline: What’s up with McDonald’s latest ad campaign in Pakistan?
summary: The giant billboards as part of McDonald’s latest ad campaign featuring host/actor/comedian Tabish Hashmi front and centre showing how the fast food giant uses local ingredients and contributes billions to Pakistan’s economy had me thinking: what’s up with that?McDonald’s Pakistan is making a concerted pitch about its local roots. Is it simply celebrating 28 years in the country, or is there a bigger reason the brand wants consumers to look beyond the burgers? And could the boycott have something to do with it?The brand wants customers to think about the farmers growing its potatoes and fresh greens, the poultry and dairy partners supplying ingredients, and the network of local businesses that help keep its restaurants running.It is an interesting shift in emphasis. Rather than simply selling the familiar appeal of burgers, fries and Happy Meals, McDonald’s is selling a bigger story: that buying from the brand also supports Pakistani businesses, workers and communities.And it has numbers to back up that argument.The economic contribution pitchAccording to an Oxford Economics study highlighted on McDonald’s Pakistan’sShana Bashana campaign page, the company contributed Rs22.6 billion to Pakistan’s gross domestic product (GDP) and supported an estimated 13,900 jobs. Between July 2024 and June 2025, it spent Rs15.1 billion with Pakistan-based suppliers, representing 91% of its total supplier spend. The company also reports Rs5.9 billion in sustained tax contributions.Its local network includes 55 vendors, covering 29 food suppliers and 26 non-food partners. The local sourcing message is particularly important. McDonald’s is pointing out that its fries do not simply arrive from some distant global supply chain: Pakistani agricultural partners help grow the potatoes used in them. Its campaign also highlights locally sourced greens, poultry and dairy.There is a distinction worth making, however. The 91% figure refers to spending with Pakistan-based suppliers, not to 91% of all ingredients being locally produced. Still, the figures offer a substantive case for the brand’s economic footprint.Is the boycott behind the campaign?McDonald’s has faced boycott calls in Pakistan and other Muslim-majority markets. McDonald's Pakistan's new campaign highlights its local sourcing and economic contributions, likely a strategic response to boycotts and growing local competition.

The giant billboards as part of McDonald’s latest ad campaign featuring host/actor/comedian Tabish Hashmi front and centre showing how the fast food giant uses local ingredients and contributes billions to Pakistan’s economy had me thinking: what’s up with that?

McDonald’s Pakistan is making a concerted pitch about its local roots. Is it simply celebrating 28 years in the country, or is there a bigger reason the brand wants consumers to look beyond the burgers? And could the boycott have something to do with it?

The brand wants customers to think about the farmers growing its potatoes and fresh greens, the poultry and dairy partners supplying ingredients, and the network of local businesses that help keep its restaurants running.

It is an interesting shift in emphasis. Rather than simply selling the familiar appeal of burgers, fries and Happy Meals, McDonald’s is selling a bigger story: that buying from the brand also supports Pakistani businesses, workers and communities.

And it has numbers to back up that argument.

According to an Oxford Economics study highlighted on McDonald’s Pakistan’sShana Bashana campaign page, the company contributed Rs22.6 billion to Pakistan’s gross domestic product (GDP) and supported an estimated 13,900 jobs. Between July 2024 and June 2025, it spent Rs15.1 billion with Pakistan-based suppliers, representing 91% of its total supplier spend. The company also reports Rs5.9 billion in sustained tax contributions.

Its local network includes 55 vendors, covering 29 food suppliers and 26 non-food partners. The local sourcing message is particularly important. McDonald’s is pointing out that its fries do not simply arrive from some distant global supply chain: Pakistani agricultural partners help grow the potatoes used in them. Its campaign also highlights locally sourced greens, poultry and dairy.

There is a distinction worth making, however. The 91% figure refers to spending with Pakistan-based suppliers, not to 91% of all ingredients being locally produced. Still, the figures offer a substantive case for the brand’s economic footprint.

McDonald’s has faced boycott calls in Pakistan and other Muslim-majority markets. Images of Israel Defense Forces (IDF) soldiers receiving McDonald’s meals became a major source of controversy. The global company subsequently faced reputational pressure across several markets.

Pakistan was no exception. A 2024 news report cited market sources who said McDonald’s and other international fast-food brands had experienced noticeable business declines amid boycott-related consumer sentiment. A 2025 news report also described significant initial sales pressure on McDonald’s and KFC, with some franchises reportedly seeing sales fall by as much as 40%.

That is evidence that the boycott had a real commercial impact at the time. It is not evidence that McDonald’s Pakistan is currently experiencing falling sales, though. The company has not publicly provided current local sales figures that would establish whether its business is still suffering.

So, is the new campaign an attempt to win customers back? It is a plausible interpretation. If consumers increasingly associate an international brand with a political controversy, reminding them that its local operations support Pakistani farmers and workers offers an alternative way to think about the business.

It also gives customers a different consideration: boycotting the brand may affect not only the franchise operator but also local suppliers and employees who depend on its business. That does not settle the ethical debate, but it changes the terms of the conversation.

The local sourcing message may also be a response to a broader change in consumer sentiment. The boycott encouraged some Pakistanis to explore domestic alternatives, from soft drinks to fast food. For an international chain, demonstrating local roots could help counter the perception that choosing a Pakistani alternative is necessarily the more patriotic decision.

McDonald’s is effectively arguing that a global brand and a local economic footprint are not mutually exclusive. Its restaurants are locally operated, and its supply chain includes Pakistani businesses. The campaign asks consumers to see those connections as part of the value of the brand.

There is also a straightforward marketing explanation. Marking 28 years in Pakistan provides a natural occasion to celebrate suppliers and highlight economic impact. The campaign may be intended to strengthen brand affinity, distinguish McDonald’s from competitors and remind customers why the chain has remained part of the market for nearly three decades.

These explanations are not mutually exclusive. A campaign can celebrate genuine local partnerships while also trying to repair a brand’s image and encourage customers to return.

There is another factor McDonald’s cannot ignore: Pakistan has developed a much more diverse fast-food market, with local burger businesses offering compelling alternatives.

Home-grown chains have helped build a market where consumers have more choices than the familiar international franchises. Independent burger joints and newer local operators can compete through distinctive flavours, generous portions, localised menus, pricing and delivery offers. Reporting during the boycott also documented consumers shifting towards local food businesses.

This is not necessarily a story of local brands replacing McDonald’s outright. Global chains retain advantages in brand recognition, consistency, established supply chains and promotions. But the local competition gives customers more reasons to experiment — and more alternatives if they decide not to visit McDonald’s.

The result is a tougher question for the brand: what makes it worth choosing over a Pakistani competitor?

Its answer appears to be a combination of familiarity, product consistency and now, a stronger story about its contribution to the country.

Still, the timing invites speculation. The boycott may have weakened some consumers’ attachment to the brand, while a stronger local fast-food sector has given them more alternatives. Both could make it more important for McDonald’s to demonstrate why it belongs in Pakistan.

What is clear is that McDonald’s wants customers to see more than a global logo: it wants them to see Pakistani farmers, suppliers, employees and businesses behind the meal.

Whether that is enough to win back customers who have moved on — for political reasons, better local options or simply changing tastes — remains to be seen.

The Pakistan Textile Council urges the Prime Minister to maintain the Export Facilitation Scheme for all textile inputs, warning that further exclusions of yarns and fabrics will severely harm value-added exports and competitiveness.

The Pakistan Textile Council (PTC) has urged Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif to retain the Export Facilitation Scheme (EFS) for all legitimate export inputs and reject further exclusions of yarns and fabrics, warning that such restrictions could undermine Pakistan’s value-added textile exports.

In a letter to the prime minister, PTC Chairman Fawad Anwar opposed demands to exclude all yarns and fabrics falling under Chapters 52 and 55 of the Pakistan Customs Tariff from the scheme. The council also sent copies of the letter to the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) chairman and the secretary of commerce.

The council appreciated the government’s efforts to curb misdeclaration and misuse of the EFS but said further exclusions would hurt exporters supplying international markets.

“Accepting these demands would cause serious and lasting harm to Pakistan’s value-added exports,” Anwar said in the letter.

The PTC noted that the government had already removed raw cotton, cotton yarn and grey cloth from the scheme in 2025 through SRO 1359(I)/2025. It said the latest demands contradicted the understanding reached during earlier consultations that no further exclusions would be sought.

Highlighting shifts in global textile demand, the council cited Textile Exchange’s Materials Market Report 2025, which found that synthetic fibres accounted for 69 percent of global fibre production in 2024, while cotton’s share stood at 19 percent.

Man-made fibre (MMF)-based products account for around 63 percent of global textile and apparel trade, compared with approximately 12 percent of Pakistan’s textile and apparel exports, according to the PTC.

The council said competing countries were expanding their presence in the segment, noting that Bangladesh aimed to increase the share of MMF in its apparel exports from around 24 percent to 40 percent by 2030.

Pakistan has almost no domestic viscose or lyocell fibre production, while its polyester value chain faces cost and scale disadvantages compared with Chinese and Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) producers, the letter stated.

As a result, value-added exporters depend on imported MMF yarns and fabrics, many of which are specified by international buyers, to secure and fulfil orders.

The PTC warned that the 2025 exclusions had already forced exporters to pay taxes upfront on affected inputs, increasing liquidity pressures and production costs. Further restrictions on yarns and fabrics under Chapters 52 and 55 could raise input costs, tie up working capital and discourage investment in value-added and MMF-based production capacity.

The council also cautioned that the proposed exclusions could weaken international buyers’ confidence in Pakistan as a reliable sourcing destination.

On concerns about misuse of the scheme, the PTC backed strict action against misdeclaration, under-invoicing and diversion of imports into the domestic market. It said the FBR and Pakistan Customs had the legal powers, systems and personnel to identify and prosecute offenders, adding that recent detections demonstrated the effectiveness of enforcement measures.

“The misuse of a few cannot justify penalising genuine exporters or dismantling a scheme that is central to export competitiveness,” Anwar said.

The council urged the prime minister to ensure that the EFS remained available for all legitimate export inputs, with no further exclusions of yarns and fabrics under Chapters 52 and 55.

It also called for stronger enforcement through input-output coefficient audits, reconciliation of scheme imports with export documents, risk-based examinations and strict penalties for offenders.

Instead of taxing imported inputs, the PTC proposed addressing concerns of domestic suppliers by restoring zero-rating on local supplies of inputs to EFS users.

The council said textiles and apparel remained Pakistan’s largest export sector and that its growth depended on competitive access to the inputs demanded by global markets. It reaffirmed its willingness to work with the government to prevent misuse while protecting legitimate exporters and foreign exchange earnings.

LONDON: Britain’s Prince William turned one of London’s most famous thoroughfares, The Mall leading to Buckingham Palace, into a temporary cricket pitch on Tuesday, where he was joined by some of the game’s biggest names to promote his Earthshot climate prize.

The wide red-paved promenade in the heart of the city is more often seen as the setting for grand royal processions and patriotic flag-waving celebrations.

But on Tuesday, William picked up a cricket bat for an informal game with current and former international players including ex-Indian captain Sourav Ganguly, West Indies legend Brian Lara and England captain Joe Root.

Against the palatial backdrop, William - dressed in a shirt and sweater - clubbed away a series of gentle deliveries from Ganguly and posed for selfies with onlookers.

“He batted alright,” said Ganguly when asked for his verdict on the prince’s skills.

The event was designed to celebrate the ties between Britain and India - two passionate cricketing nations - as India prepares to host the annual summit and awards ceremony of William’s Earthshot Prize next month.

The prize, founded in 2020, honours five winners with £1 million ($1.32 million) each to scale solutions aimed at repairing the planet.

Pakistan's Finance Minister reaffirmed national ownership of IMF-supported reforms in taxation, energy, SOEs, and pensions, stressing sustained implementation for economic growth and public welfare.

Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb reaffirmed on Tuesday Pakistan’s ownership of taxation, energy, state-owned enterprise (SOE) and pension reforms under the IMF-supported programme, stressing that sustained implementation was essential to achieve lasting economic growth and public welfare.

The development came as the minister highlighted debt management and fiscal reforms at a panel on Mitigating Sovereign Risks in Market-Access Countries on the sidelines of the World Bank Group–IMF Annual Meetings 2026 in Bangkok, Thailand, according to a Finance Division statement.

“The Finance minister reaffirmed national ownership of taxation, energy, state-owned enterprises and pension reforms under the IMF-supported programme. He stressed the sustained reform implementation to translate macroeconomic stability into sustainable growth and public welfare,” the statement read.

The minister further highlighted Pakistan’s progress in fiscal consolidation, reducing inflation and rebuilding foreign exchange reserves.

“He emphasised revenue mobilisation, tax administration reforms, expenditure restraint and privatisation to strengthen economic resilience,” the statement read.

Aurangzeb outlined debt management measures to lower financing costs, extend maturities and reduce rollover risks. He noted that renewed market access supports a strategy to improve the external debt profile without increasing the overall size.

Finance minister discusses Mashreq Bank’s expansion

Federal minister Aurangzeb also met with Mashreq Bank’s senior management to discuss its expanding presence in Pakistan, a separate Finance Division statement said.

The minister highlighted macroeconomic gains and renewed market access, reaffirming support for Mashreq’s expansion and sustainable growth. He reviewed digital banking growth and opportunities to advance financial inclusion through technology and microfinance.

“Discussion also covered expanding offshore service operations, drawing on Pakistan’s skilled workforce. The meeting explored digital accounts for overseas Pakistanis, foreign-currency products and wider outreach across the GCC.” the statement read.

He also discussed collaboration on tokenisation, blockchain, and digital assets within Pakistan’s evolving regulatory framework. He reviewed potential support for Sukuk, further Panda bond issuance and innovative financing under Pakistan’s medium-term debt strategy.

article_text:
Most Gulf bourses closedhigher on Tuesday, with Saudi Arabia’s benchmark index snapping a four-session losing streak, even as the kingdom extended the closure of Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport until Saturday.

A spokesperson for the Saudi-led coalition said on Tuesday that civilians would soon be warned to evacuate a site in Yemen’s Sanaa ahead of a special operation.

The Saudi index rose 0.3%, helped by a 1.8% gain in Saudi National Bank, the country’s biggest lender by assets. That recovered part of the bank’s 1.2% drop on Monday.

Elsewhere, Dubai’s main share index gained 0.4%, while the Abu Dhabi index rose 0.3%.

GCC markets traded in a tight range on Tuesday as investors weighed rising regional risks. The lack of clarity on US-Iran talks and continued disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz kept sentiment cautious, although de-escalation efforts helped prevent a deeper sell-off, said Daniel Takieddine, co-founder and CEO, Sky Links Capital Group.

In Qatar, the index added 0.2%, building on a rebound after hitting its lowest level in more than six years on Sunday.

Airlines have cancelled flights after attacks by Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthis emptied the skies over the Saudi capital. Qatar Airways said on Monday it had temporarily suspended flights to and from Riyadh and Dammam due to the situation.

UAE presidential adviser Anwar Gargash said on Monday there was a pressing need to revive joint Gulf action, particularly on security and defence. He said targeting Saudi Arabia undermined the security of all Gulf states.

Offering some reassurance on energy security, Energy Minister Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman said on Monday that Saudi Arabia wants to raise its pipeline crude export capacity to as much as 10 million barrels per day.

The plan involves repurposing a domestic gas pipeline and investing in the existing East-West network, which carries crude to the Red Sea and avoids the Strait of Hormuz.

Outside the Gulf, Egypt’s blue-chip index dropped 0.7%.

Egypt’s current account deficit widened to $7.9 billion in the April–June 2026 quarter, compared with $2.2 billion in the corresponding quarter of the previous year, the central bank said on Monday.

WASHINGTON: President Donald Trump said late on Monday he did not believe that China and Russia were helping Iran “at all,” adding that Moscow and Beijing had “too much to lose” if they enabled Tehran.

Trump said on Truth Social that he had seen comments from his critics and opponents that China and Russia were helping Iran.

“If they are, it’s at a very low level, but I don’t believe they are at all. They have too much to lose, and we would know about it, and know about it very fast,” Trump wrote.

Trump said in July he trusted China and Russia not to help Tehran in the Iran war, but warned that if they did get involved “it would be very bad for them.”

The United States and Iran have been at war since February 28, when ​the US and Israel attacked Iran and Tehran responded with its own strikes on Israel and Gulf states that host US bases. US-Israeli strikes on Iran and ​Israeli attacks on Lebanon have since killed thousands and displaced millions.

Trump says US will not attack Iran before midterm elections in November

Trump has previously described Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin as “neutral” during the Iran war.

Iranian drone attacks on CIA facilities in the Gulf have prompted US intelligence analysts to investigate whether Russia provided targeting information or ​advanced drone technology. European foreign ministers pressed the case in a March meeting with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio. The Washington Post and the Wall Street Journal that month reported that Russia was providing Iran with targeting information.

Moscow and Beijing maintain close ties with Tehran. Russia has said the Iran war could lead to a nuclear arms race in the Middle East. Beijing has condemned Washington’s attacks on Tehran as a brazen violation of Iran’s sovereignty.

Last month, Trump warned Xi against providing support to Iran when the Chinese leader visited Washington, and received assurances that China would not do so, the US ambassador to China said at the time.

Trump defends Russia diesel deal as lawmakers from both parties complain

The warning came amid reports that China had supplied Iran with shoulder-fired ​air-defense missile launchers and that Tehran had found ways to evade sanctions on its oil sales with Chinese ​help.

In September, Trump brushed aside a report that Iran acquired satellite images of a base in Jordan from Chinese entities before an attack that killed three US troops there in July.

headline: Influential Hindu group urges India to block Starlink amid Musk-Ambani feud

BENGALURU: An influential Hindu nationalist group close to India’s ruling party urged the government on Tuesday to block Elon Musk’s Starlink from launching satellite internet services in the country, citing national security concerns.

Starlink’s four-year wait to launch in India has come under renewed scrutiny after Musk last week accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s government and billionaire Mukesh Ambani of stalling its entry to favour Ambani’s Reliance Jio.

India’s communications ministry said last week that security assessments were under way for Starlink and rival satellite ventures backed by Reliance Jio and Bharti Airtel. It described suggestions the approval process was unfair or discriminatory as “baseless and misconceived”.

The call for Starlink’s ban came from Swadeshi Jagran Manch (SJM), the economic wing of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS), the Hindu nationalist organisation that is the ideological parent of Modi’s ruling Bharatiya Janata Party.

India rejects monopoly claim after Musk accuses Ambani of blocking Starlink launch

SJM also linked its demand to trade tensions with the US. If Washington imposes high tariffs on Indian imports “in the name of national security, then India is certainly within its rights to block Starlink based on its genuine national security concerns,” national co-convenor Ashwani Mahajan said in a statement.

Starlink’s technology could make it difficult for authorities to restrict internet services during security emergencies and ensure Indian internet traffic passes through domestic infrastructure, Mahajan added.

SJM has influenced Indian policy in recent years, notably pushing for rules to protect small traders from US-owned e-commerce firms Amazon and Walmart’s Flipkart.

SpaceX, Starlink’s parent company, did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Market with more than a billion internet users

Starlink is seeking to launch in a country with more than a billion internet subscribers. Alongside Starlink, satellite ventures backed by Reliance Jio and Bharti are awaiting final clearances to begin services.

Musk has repeatedly taunted Ambani on X, questioning why Starlink still lacked a licence despite what he said were years of compliance with Indian requirements.

“Is Ambani the real boss of India?” he posted last week, as he accused the rival billionaire of stalling Starlink’s entry.

Pakistan successfully test-fired its extended-range Fatah-2 hypersonic ballistic missile, equipped with advanced navigation and maneuverability to defeat enemy defenses.

Pakistan Army has successfully test-fired the extended-range version of its Fatah-2 hypersonic ballistic missile, the military’s media wing said on Tuesday.

According to a statement issued by the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), the weapon system is equipped with advanced navigation and state-of-the-art avionics, enabling it to engage targets with high precision.

The ISPR said the missile’s unique trajectory and manoeuvrability features enable it to defeat enemy missile defence systems, while its extended range further enhances the army’s capability to engage targets deep inside enemy territory.

The test was witnessed by the Commander of the Army Rocket Force Command, senior Pakistan Army officers, and scientists and engineers involved in the programme.

The commander appreciated the dedication and technical expertise of the scientists and engineers, the statement added.

President Asif Ali Zardari, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Chief of Army Staff and Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Asim Munir, and the services chiefs congratulated the scientists and engineers on the successful test launch.

Separately, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi congratulated the nation on the test, describing it as a significant development in the country’s defence sector.

He said Pakistan Army scientists and engineers had achieved a commendable feat.

Pakistan's PM urged Europe to expand legal migration for skilled workers, citing mutual benefits and anti-smuggling efforts. An EU Commissioner praised Pakistan's significant reduction in illegal migration.

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Tuesday called for expanding legal migration opportunities for Pakistani skilled workers and professionals in Europe, saying such pathways could help meet European labour-market needs while protecting prospective migrants from smuggling networks.

The prime minister made these remarks during a meeting with European Union Commissioner for Internal Affairs and Migration Magnus Brunner, who called on him in Islamabad during his first visit to Pakistan, the PM Office said.

Highlighting Pakistan’s efforts to combat irregular migration, migrant smuggling and human trafficking through legislative reforms, stronger institutions, effective enforcement and international cooperation, Shehbaz emphasized: “Efforts to address irregular migration should be complemented by practical opportunities for safe, orderly, and regular migration.”

The prime minister reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to strengthening its partnership with the European Union and cooperation across all pillars of the Pakistan-EU Strategic Engagement Plan 2019. Migration and mobility are among the plan’s eight pillars.

Commissioner Brunner appreciated the measures taken by Pakistan and the cooperation extended by its government.

He expressed confidence that these efforts would help expand legal migration pathways and promote mutually beneficial labour mobility between Pakistan and the European Union.

Earlier, during a meeting with Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi in Islamabad, European Commissioner Brunner praised Pakistan’s measures to combat illegal migration.

Brunner said Pakistan’s effective measures have resulted in a commendable 64% reduction in illegal migration to Europe.

He also commended the Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) for demonstrating professional capabilities despite limited resources. He said reducing illegal migration will open up pathways for legal migration.

Naqvi said Pakistan has adopted a zero-tolerance policy against illegal migration. “Following a 64% reduction in illegal migration, our next target is to eliminate it completely,” he said.

The minister stressed the need for Pakistan and the European Union to work together to completely eliminate illegal migration.

During the meeting, the two sides discussed promoting legal migration between Pakistan and the European Union and expanding opportunities for skilled workers.

Both sides agreed to enhance cooperation in border security and promote legal immigration. They also agreed to further strengthen collaboration in migration, institutional cooperation and border management.

Around 7,900 people died or disappeared on migration routes in 2025, taking the total dead and missing since 2014 beyond 80,000, the United Nations’ migration agency said in a statement on April 21.

The UN’s International Organization for Migration said people were being forced into dangerous, irregular journeys when safe pathways were out of reach, and urged countries to find the political will to save more lives on migration routes.

The deaths or disappearance of around “7,900 people were documented on global migration routes worldwide in 2025”, the IOM said.

The IOM’s Missing Migrants Project “has documented more than 80,000 deaths and disappearances during migration since 2014,” the agency said.

“While these figures represent only the lowest boundary of the true number of affected people, they nonetheless underscore the need for urgent action to end migrant deaths and address the complex needs of families left behind,” said the IOM.

A Saudi-led coalition urged civilians on Tuesday to evacuate the Yemen Oil Company’s Sabah central station in the capital Sanaa ahead of a planned military operation.

A statement from the coalition’s joint forces command identified the site on a map and said civilians should leave the area for their own safety.

A spokesperson for Yemen’s Houthis, Yahya Saree, warned that any strikes on Sanaa would be met with a “harsh and painful” response in the Saudi capital Riyadh.

Houthis also warned employees and civilians near Saudi Aramco oil facilities to evacuate and stay away, saying the facilities were legitimate targets for their forces.

Houthis claim attack targeting Riyadh airport with ballistic missile

Fighting has escalated between the Saudi-led coalition and the Houthis, who have been attacking Saudi airports and oil facilities since last week in a spillover from the wider regional conflagration between the US and Iran.

Saudi Arabia has in recent weeks launched strikes against the Houthis and is backing a Yemeni government counteroffensive after the group seized strategic territory along the Red Sea coast last month.

The conflict has disrupted air travel in Saudi Arabia, with Riyadh airport remaining closed after a deadly missile strike on Saturday claimed by the Houthis.

article_text:
A constitutional petition seeks the immediate recovery of non-functional KP Chief Minister Sohail Afridi, allegedly abducted from his official residence, citing grave constitutional and human rights violations.

A constitutional petition has been filed in the Peshawar High Court (PHC) seeking the immediate recovery of non-functional Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi, whose brother alleges he was abducted from the Chief Minister’s House and is being held in illegal custody.

The petition was filed by Muhammad Aamir, the non-functional KP chief minister’s brother, who urged the court to take immediate action, order Afridi’s recovery and direct authorities to produce him before the court, read a statement shared by Sohail Afridi’s Facebook page.

The petitioner alleged that armed and masked men took away the elected chief minister in the presence of the Capital City Police Officer (CCPO) Peshawar. He said the alleged abduction and detention violated the Constitution, the law and fundamental human rights.

The petition maintains that Afridi’s life and liberty are at serious risk and that his continued detention, along with the lack of information about his whereabouts, raises grave constitutional concerns. It cites Articles 4, 9, 10 and 14 of the Constitution.

The petitioner has asked the court to direct the CCPO Peshawar to submit complete details of the alleged incident and the security arrangements in place at the time. He has also sought an explanation of his brother’s whereabouts, who is holding him and under what legal authority.

The petition further seeks an independent and impartial investigation into the alleged abduction, the identification of those involved and action against them in accordance with the law.

It also asks the court to order the immediate preservation of CCTV footage, security records and other evidence related to the incident, and direct police officials to submit a detailed report on steps taken to recover the chief minister.

The petitioner has urged the high court to ensure Afridi’s safety, liberty and protection, warning that any delay in addressing the matter could endanger his life. He has requested that the petition be fixed for an urgent hearing.

PM Shehbaz Sharif announced the government will set wheat prices after provincial consultations, aiming for fair farmer returns and consumer affordability, while emphasizing agricultural growth and food security.

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif said on Tuesday that the government will announce the wheat price after consultations with the provinces, stressing that the decision must ensure fair returns for farmers while keeping wheat affordable for consumers.

Chairing the first meeting of the National Agriculture and Food Security Council (NAFSC) in Islamabad on Tuesday, the prime minister said determining the wheat price before the start of sowing was essential to compensate farmers adequately for their efforts.

He said the country had sufficient wheat stocks to meet domestic requirements and warned that those involved in hoarding the commodity would not be given any concession.

The prime minister said agriculture was the backbone of Pakistan’s economy and had the potential to put the country on a growth trajectory in the short term.

He said the federal government would extend all possible support to the provinces to promote agricultural development, adding that providing farmers with fertilisers at affordable rates, quality seeds, modern machinery and equipment and technical expertise for efficient water use was a priority.

Shehbaz also emphasised ensuring fair prices for crops, particularly for small and medium-sized farmers.

Highlighting the potential of the livestock sector, he said it could significantly boost the country’s exports. He added that the government was taking steps to increase exports of Pakistani halal meat.

The prime minister appreciated Punjab’s initiatives for farmers, including aquaculture, shrimp farming and direct subsidies through the Kisan Card. He also acknowledged the Sindh government’s efforts to support farmers and improve access to facilities.

During the meeting, Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif and Sindh Food Minister Makhdoom Mahboob-uz-Zaman briefed participants on their respective provincial governments’ initiatives for farmers and agricultural development.

The meeting was also briefed on measures to promote agriculture in Balochistan, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Azad Jammu and Kashmir, and Gilgit-Baltistan.

Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, federal ministers Rana Tanveer Hussain, Musadik Malik, Jam Kamal Khan, Ahsan Iqbal and Attaullah Tarar, among other federal officials and advisers, attended the meeting.

article_text:
MUMBAI: Indian government bonds snapped a four-session falling streak on Tuesday, after the yield rising to a three-year high attracted investors back to the market.

A policy rate hike and liquidity withdrawal by the central bank had pushed the benchmark bond yield up by 20 basis points over four sessions. The 6.94% 2036 bond ended at 7.3655% against 7.3857% in the previous session.

The rupee outperformed its regional peers and ended 0.5% up against the dollar at 95.28, boosted by new central bank measures to alleviate pressure on the Asian currency and likely spot market intervention that magnified their impact.

“The base case is that the 10-year bond yield has provided support in the 7.40% ranges, however, any further OMO (open market operation) sale could push the 10-year benchmark yield towards the 7.60–7.65% range,” said Harsimran Sahni, associate director and head of treasury at Anand Rathi Global Finance.

India’s state borrowing costs spike to over six-year high as demand fades

The RBI raised its key policy rate by 25 basis points last week and changed its policy stance, hinting at more hikes in coming months. The central bank has also announced currency market measures that cloud the outlook for banking system liquidity and impact banks’ treasury operations.

Bets of a December rate increase have hardened after consumer inflation accelerated to 5.54% in September, while the benchmark Brent crude contract held above the $105 per barrel mark.

Bond gains were curbed by hefty supply.

Indian states raised over 300 billion rupees through bonds while the Reserve Bank of India sold notes worth 250 billion rupees through an open market operation. New Delhi is sue to sell benchmark note worth 340 billion rupees on Friday.

Traders awaited US inflation data due on Wednesday for cues on the Federal Reserve’s moves.

Overnight indexed swap rates eased, tracking bond yields and a pullback in US Treasury yields.

The one-year OIS rate ended at 6.3350%, while the two-year rate closed at 6.5150%, and the most liquid five-year rate settled lower at 6.74%.

DURBAN: Australia paceman Josh Hazlewood bowled his side to a 214-run victory on the last day of the first Test at Kingsmead on Tuesday with South Africa’s resistance ending before tea as the home side were dismissed for 206.

Hazlewood took 6-49 as Australia bagged the six wickets they needed on the last day to go 1-0 up in the three-match series.

He struck twice in one over with the newft ball after already having taken two wickets on Monday and then breaking through South Africa’s stoic early fightback on Tuesday.

The 35-year-old Hazlewood also removed the last batsman to ensure the victory in the first clash between the teams since South Africa upset Australia in last year’s World Test Championship final at Lord’s in London.

South Africa held out for the first 110 minutes of Tuesday’s play before a legside delivery from Hazlewood was edged by Wiaan Mulder and snagged by a diving catch from wicketkeeper Alex Carey.

Mulder and Aiden Markram resumed at 102-4 overnight and the pair extended the fifth-wicket partnership to a patient 69 runs off 205 balls before Hazlewood’s breakthrough with Mulder making 29.

Part-time spinner Matt Renshaw, who was the man of the match for Australia with the bat, then took a second Test wicket when Kyle Verreynne quickly followed Mulder back to the change room with a reckless shot that saw him caught at slip by Steve Smith without scoring.

South Africa were 166-6 at lunch and added 25 runs before the new ball was taken but crumbled quickly thereafter.

Hazlewood thencompleted the win as tailender Anrich Nortje popped up the ball to short midwicket for Nathan Lyon to catch.

Former Australia captain Smith, who did not field in Monday’s late session after a blow to the head while batting, returned to action on Tuesday.

“Steve Smith has undergone a series of clinical assessments over the past 24 hours in accordance with Cricket Australia’s concussion protocols and has been cleared to take the field this morning,” a statement said.

MUMBAI: The flagship firm of India’s Adani group, Adani Enterprises, plans to raise around 20 billion rupees ($210 million) through the sale of short-duration bonds, two merchant bankers directly aware of the transaction said on Tuesday.

“The company would look for an issuance of below five-year maturity, and may aim to complete the sale within this quarter,” one of the bankers said.

The company last tapped private corporate debt in October 2025, when it raised 10 billion rupees through the sale of bonds maturing in two years and six months at a semi-annual coupon of 8.70%.
