MUMBAI: Borrowing costs for the most liquid part of India’s state government bond curve breached the 8% handle for the first time in over six years on Tuesday, according to traders, tracking a sharp spike in central government yields and weakening investor appetite.

Indian states raised over 300 billion rupees ($3.15 billion) through a sale of bonds, of which 9- to 10-year state bonds were sold in the 8.03%-8.10% range.

This is the first time since April 2020 that yields on state government bonds with a 10-year maturity have broken 8%.

Yields on other ultra-long papers were between 8.14% and 8.21%.

“The rise in state debt yields reflects a combination of elevated crude oil prices, tighter liquidity conditions, and open market sales,” said Harsimran Sahni, associate director and head of treasury at Anand Rathi Global Finance.

Last week, states raised funds through 9- to 10-year bonds in the 7.91%-7.93% band.

The benchmark 10-year 6.94% 2036 bond yield was at 7.36% on Tuesday, up from 7.19% last week.

India bonds rise as investors see value after 10-year yield nears 7.40%

The yield spread of 10-year state bonds over central government bonds has compressed from around 75 basis points to about 65 bps in the last two months, and “we expect it to remain in the 55-70 bps range in the near term,” Sahni added.

Indian states aim to raise over 3.6 trillion rupees through bonds this quarter, after raising 5 trillion rupees in the first half of the fiscal.

England on Tuesday named their squads for November’s white-ball tour of Australia, with all-rounder Jacob Bethell returning from a knee injury as they step up preparations for next year’s One Day International World Cup.

Bethell, who was injured during England’s ODI series win over India in July, has been selected in both the ODI and T20 squads.

Jofra Archer also returns for the ODI series after being rested for this month’s tri-series in Pakistan, while uncapped bowler Eddie Jack and 18-year-old wicketkeeper-batter Thomas Rew are among those who earned their maiden senior England call-ups in the T20 squad.

Wicketkeeper-batter Phil Salt returns after a quad injury ruled him out of England’s 3-0 T20 series sweep of Sri Lanka last month.

Wicketkeeper-batter Jos Buttler remains sidelined as he begins rehabilitation following hamstring surgery, while fast bowler Saqib Mahmood misses out with a knee injury.

England increase central contracts to record 39

Archer and fellow quicks Gus Atkinson, Sonny Baker and Josh Tongue will leave the tour after the three-match ODI series as England manage their workloads ahead of the Test tour of South Africa in December.

The Australia series forms part of England’s build-up to next year’s ODI World Cup in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia.

headline: SE Fruits and Vegetable to refile IPO application with additional disclosures
summary: SE Fruits and Vegetable Limited will withdraw its existing initial public offering (IPO) application and submit a fresh one with additional disclosures about the transition of its underlying business from a partnership to a public limited company, the company said on Tuesday.“The Board of Directors of SE Fruits and Vegetable Limited has decided to withdraw the Company’s current IPO application and submit a fresh application after incorporating additional disclosures into the prospectus,” the company said in a statement.“The additional disclosures will provide further information regarding the transition of the underlying business from a partnership organisation, operating since 1998, to the newly incorporated Public Limited Company in 2026,” it added.Sources familiar with the matter said the application was being withdrawn after concerns emerged over disclosures that had not been adequately included in the IPO documents.The omissions came to the attention of regulators, prompting the company to resubmit its application with the required information, the sources toldBusiness Recorder.“The Board considers the resubmission to be in the interests of transparency, regulatory compliance, investor protection and informed investment decision-making,” SE Fruits said, adding that it remained committed to accessing Pakistan’s capital markets.“The withdrawal is a procedural step and does not represent an abandonment of the company’s IPO plans. SE Fruits remains committed to accessing Pakistan’s capital markets and intends to reapply after completing the revised prospectus and applicable regulatory process,” it said.SE Fruits, Vegs secures SECP approval for IPOSE Fruits and Vegetables Limited, formerly known as Shaheen Enterprises, is a Punjab-based horticulture exporter specialising in mangoes, citrus (kinnow), and potatoes, along with other agricultural produce.As of FY2026, SE Fruits and Vegetables reported a topline of approximately $7.6 million and export revenue of about $4 million. Its net revenue for FY2026 was Rs2.133 billion, with a profit after tax of Rs303.8 million, and it has been debt-free since FY2024. The company held less than a 2% market share in national fruit and vegetable exports in FY2026.In 2026, SE Fruits and Vegetables became the first fresh fruit and vegetable company to prepare for listing on the Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) through an Initial Public Offering (IPO). The IPO aims to raise between Rs1.2 billion and Rs1.92 billion to fund working capital, expand processing and export operations, establish international offices in the UAE and Uzbekistan, and invest in enterprise resource planning, asset-tracking systems, and solar energy.

Copper pricesrose for a third straight session on Tuesday as persistent concerns over a supply shortage kept the metal within striking distance of an all-time peak.

Benchmark three-month copper on the London Metal Exchange was up 0.1% at $14,636.50 a metric ton as of 0915 GMT, close to the record $14,875 seen last month.

Supply concerns remained in focus after Chile’s Codelco partially suspended operations at its El Teniente mine following a landslide, while Antofagasta’s Centinela copper mine and two unions were set to resume talks as a strike continued.

“Copper continues to benefit from physical-market tightness and declining exchange inventories, helping it withstand the firm dollar better than the wider complex,” Sucden Financial said in a note.

A stronger greenback makes dollar-denominated metals more expensive for holders of other currencies. The dollar took a breather on Tuesday but hovered near an 18-month high.

All reported copper mine disruptions for 2025-26 — including at Indonesia’s Grasberg mine and Kamoa-Kakula in the Democratic Republic of Congo — amount to 350,000-400,000 tons per year of contained copper, which equates to only 30%-50% of published disruption allowances, Panmure Liberum said.

“Therefore, the dominant price driver is probably speculative/financial,” the bank added in a note.

A disruption allowance is a percentage of mine production that analysts assume will be lost due to unplanned events in a given year.

LME copper stocks declined by 1,625 tons to 232,275 tons, leaving inventories outside the US tight. The cash LME copper contract was trading at a $181.50 premium to the three-month forward, indicating scarce near-term availability.

Aluminium fell 0.6% to $3,035.50 per ton, close to the eight-month low it touched on Monday. Some easing in passage restrictions in the Strait of Hormuz has reconnected Gulf smelters to the world, taking aluminium prices down, Panmure Liberum said.

New supply from Indonesia is also ramping up, with exports topping 150,000 tons in August.

Zinc lost 0.4% to $3,741.50, lead rose 0.6% to $1,894.50, nickel was flat at $15,620 and tin eased 0.2% to $53,000.

KUALA LUMPUR:Malaysian palm oil futuresreversed earlier losses to hit a more than two-week high on Tuesday, as concerns over tighter supplies next year — due to El Niño and growing biodiesel demand — outweighed pressure from currently high stockpiles.

The benchmark palm oil contract for December delivery on the Bursa Malaysia Derivatives Exchange rose 45 ringgit, or 0.97%, to 4,682 ringgit ($1,146.43) a metric ton, the highest closing price since September 24.

The bearish September stocks are already reflected in the market as it had already weakened before and after the release of the Malaysian Palm Oil Board’s data, said Cheang Kang Wei, agricultural commodities analyst at the Singapore-based StoneX brokerage.

Malaysia’s palm oil stockpiles in September surged to 3.51 million metric tons as production hit an all-time high, surpassing market expectations and reaching unprecedented levels.

However, Cheang said that the key question now is whether stocks can continue rising in October, noting that inventories could still remain elevated, but the pace of the build should start slowing.

Stock growth should begin moderating by November if exports hold above 1.5 million tons while production stabilises around 2.0 million tons, Cheang added. But if demand disappoints while production remains near record levels, stocks could stay above 3.5 million tons for longer and continue weighing on prices.

“The market is also increasingly looking beyond the current inventory situation and focusing on potential supply risks in 2027, including the lagged impact of El Niño and Indonesia’s growing biodiesel demand under B50,” he said.

Cargo surveyors estimated that exports of Malaysian palm oil products for October 1-10 rose between 33.5% and 37.7% from a month earlier.

Oil prices fell as traders assessed supply risks from attacks on Saudi Arabia while weighing the prospect of additional diesel supplies from Russia.

Weaker crude oil futures make palm a less attractive option for biodiesel feedstock.

Dalian’s most-active soyoil contract fell 0.65%, while its palm oil contract shed 0.77%. Soyoil prices on the Chicago Board of Trade were up 0.55%.

Palm oil tracks the price movements of rival edible oils, as it competes for a share of the global vegetable oils market.

headline: India's ICICI Life posts key quarterly margin below estimates, shares slide
summary: BENGALURU: India’s ICICI Life Insurance reported new business margins below expectations on Tuesday, sending shares sliding 3%, while second-quarter profit jumped 25% year-on-year.Its value of new business (VNB), which measures the expected profit from new policies sold, rose 24.7% on-quarter to 7.12 billion rupees.However, its VNB margin fell to 25.4% from 26.7% in the previous quarter, according to a Reuters calculation, with the shift towards higher-margin insurance products to help offset pressure from the loss of tax benefits not occurring as expected.Instead, the company’s share of higher-margin protection policies fell sequentially, while that of market-linked policies rose.At least five brokerages, including Systematix and Elara, had expected VNB margin between 25.5% and 26.5%.Prudential to sell 2% stake in ICICI Prudential AMC worth about $333 millionAnalysts expect the life insurance sector’s growth to moderate for the rest of fiscal 2027, following a surge in policy sales after the Indian government cut consumption taxes on individual life insurance premiums late last year.Growth focusICICI Life, the first major Indian life insurer to report September-quarter results, had shifted its focus towards growth over the past few quarters after prioritising margin expansion.The company’s profit grew to 3.74 billion rupees ($39.28 million) from 2.99 billion rupees a year earlier.Its net premium income rose 16.6% to 138.04 billion rupees in the September quarter.Annualised premium equivalent (APE) sales, a key measure of new business, rose 15.6% to 27.99 billion rupees, according to a Reuters calculation. NEW YORK: Apple on Tuesday is expected to show off a new round of smart home products, including an iPad-like device meant to hang on walls or perch on tabletops that will showcase its AI-upgraded Siri virtual assistant.

The devices will help users control doorbells, thermostats, and smart locks in a market where Apple has tinkered for a decade without major success. The devices could also include upgrades to its HomePod smart speaker and Apple TV devices, analysts said.

Apple is launching these products as it tries to fend off challenges from rivals, including traditional competitors like Amazon.com, which has invested heavily in its Echo speakers and Ring doorbells and last week launched premium tablets, as well as newer AI upstarts like OpenAI that have hardware ambitions of their own.

Investors are looking more closely at Apple’s hardware sales for growth as the company’s services revenue has come under regulatory pressure.

Apple cuts iPhone 18 Pro orders due to soft demand, Nikkei Asia reports

Apple first released its Home app to control smart gadgets in 2016, with HomePod smart speakers following in 2018, but those offerings are competing with Alphabet’s Google Home speakers and Amazon’s Echo line. Analysts said two major hurdles for Apple were making its devices work with a variety of third-party gadgets and the limited ability of Siri to give useful answers.

Apple this summer upgraded Siri’s capabilities with assistance from Google, but the process of wiring a smart home is still too difficult for many Apple consumers to see a benefit, said Bob O’Donnell, chief analyst at TECHnalysis Research.

“Advancements in AI should finally help, but the key questions for Apple are, do they have connectivity smarts to simplify the process, and are they going to be willing to work across the smart home ecosystem and not just within their own walled garden,” O’Donnell said.

Higher oil prices and a global bond rout weighed on European equities in recent weeks, stoking inflation fears in the energy-importing region and dimming the appeal of riskier equities.

“European equities are caught between resilient corporate earnings and rising borrowing costs,” Lauren Hyslop, investment manager at Mattioli Woods, said.

article_text:
Four people were killed and dozens injured when 14 coaches of the Rehman Baba Express derailed near Multan, Pakistan, during its journey from Karachi to Peshawar.

At least four passengers were killed and dozens others injured when 14 coaches of the Rehman Baba Express, travelling from Karachi to Peshawar, derailed near Sher Shah railway station in Multan on Tuesday.

According to a Pakistan Railways information officer, initial reports put the number of injured passengers at 30. Rescue 1122, however, reported 53 victims, including four fatalities and 49 injured people.

Rescue 1122 spokesperson Farooq Ahmad toldBusiness Recorderthat 22 of the injured were classified as having minor injuries, while 27 were shifted to medical facilities for treatment. The deceased included three women and one man.

The train was carrying nearly 1,000 passengers at the time of the accident, according to Rescue 1122.

Rescue services received the emergency call at 5:21am and deployed 11 ambulances, three fire vehicles and two rescue vehicles, with 70 rescuers taking part in the operation.

A relief train and a medical van from Multan were dispatched to the accident site. Multan divisional authorities and Rescue 1122 teams were also conducting rescue operations.

The operation was ongoing, according to Rescue 1122.

President, prime minister express concern

President Asif Ali Zardari has expressed concern over the derailment of the Rahman Baba Express near Multan, extending his heartfelt condolences to the families of passengers who lost their lives and wishing a speedy recovery to those injured.

The president directed the relevant authorities to ensure immediate assistance and provide all possible facilities to the affected passengers. He also called for a transparent investigation to determine the cause of the accident.

Meanwhile, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif took notice of the derailment of several coaches of the Rahman Baba Express in Multan and expressed sorrow over the injuries sustained by passengers.

The prime minister directed the authorities concerned to expedite rescue and relief operations and ensure that the injured receive immediate and the best possible medical treatment.

Pakistan has experienced several train accidents this year, with notable incidents resulting in fatalities and injuries, alongside broader concerns about railway safety. Pakistan Railways reported 35 train accidents in the first six months of 2026, though the overall trend showed a decline.

In March, a Lahore-bound Shalimar Express collided with a goods train near Lakha Road Railway Station in Sindh’s Naushahro Feroze district. This incident resulted in one death and 13 injuries. The collision was attributed to the interlocking system being set for a loop line where a goods train was parked, combined with a malfunctioning brake and a red signal.

An internal inspection following this incident revealed that nearly 60% of the Shalimar Express’s coaches were operating without functional brakes, with 10 out of 18 coaches having serious defects, including nine with non-functional brake cylinders.

In another incident in March, multiple bogies of the Tezgam Express, traveling from Rawalpindi to Karachi, derailed near Adam Wahan station in Lodhran. Four bogies overturned, and several others derailed, injuring 25 passengers. The exact cause of this accident was not immediately determined.

A bogie of the Shalimar Express derailed at Khanewal Junction in July while en route from Lahore to Karachi. No casualties or damage were reported, and train services resumed after repairs.

Concerns about frequent train accidents and inadequate security measures were raised by the Senate Standing Committee on Railways in February 2026. The committee noted that disciplinary action had largely focused on train drivers, with senior officers rarely held accountable, and directed the Ministry of Railways to ensure all responsible officials are proceeded against.

The National Assembly Standing Committee on Railways also sought a detailed report on the financial losses from accidents and delays in infrastructure restructuring and safety reforms.

headline: Saudi warning system stayed silent before deadly airport attacks
summary:
Saudi Arabia ceased public warnings of military attacks before deadly Riyadh airport strikes, raising concerns about vulnerability and protection, despite other Gulf nations issuing alerts.

RIYADH: S...
relevant_sector_or_market: APPAREL | COMMERCIAL BANKS | OIL & GAS / ENERGY | OIL & GAS EXPLORATION COMPANIES | PSX / EQUITIES | TECHNOLOGY & COMMUNICATION
article_text:
Saudi Arabia ceased public warnings of military attacks before deadly Riyadh airport strikes, raising concerns about vulnerability and protection, despite other Gulf nations issuing alerts.

RIYADH: Saudi Arabia stopped issuing public warnings of imminent military attacks days before a series of deadly strikes onRiyadh airportthat killed at least 18 people and wounded more than 300.

The government has not said why there were no alerts to the public before the four Riyadh attacks in the past week.

The warnings had served to highlight ​the violence undermining the kingdom’s efforts to project an image of calm to its people and the world during its war withYemen’s Houthis.

Their absence during the airport strikes raised questions about Saudi Arabia’s vulnerability to ‌attack and about its ability to protect residents and visitors, four Western and Arab officials in the region and political analysts told Reuters.

It also reflected efforts to maintain a sense of normalcy, they said.

“They (the Saudi government) want to have it both ways: to launch a military operation and at the same time try to give confidence to the population and external stakeholders,” said Sultan Alamer, a US-based Saudi academic and Senior Resident Fellow at the Middle East Policy Council think tank.

The Saudi civil defence - a national emergency management, rescue and firefighting agency which operates under the interior ministry and issues early warning alerts - and the Saudi ​government media office did not respond to emailed questions on why no alerts were issued.

Saudi Arabia’s approach is also one that some regional analysts said risked backfiring because the absence of warnings has heightened uncertainty in the kingdom.

Riyadh airport to cancel about 60% of flights on Monday after deadly attacks

On Monday, Saudi ​Arabia’s civil defence authority issued its first alerts since September 29, warning of potential threats in Riyadh and southern cities.

Reuterswas unable to ascertain whether the decision to issue alerts again was a response ⁠to the airport attacks, and the Saudi government did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the matter.

All Gulf countries have been hit by Iranian drones and missiles since theUS-Iran warbegan in February, but their governments have handled public ​warnings differently.

Qatar’s interior ministry has issued mobile phone alerts before nearly every attack, including most recent attacks in July, when residents were warned to stay inside and away from windows.

Bahrain and Kuwait have repeatedly sounded sirens urging people to take shelter.

Saudi Arabia began issuing threat alerts ​to mobile phones and social media accounts via a national early warning system in May.

But despite increasing Houthi attacks leading up to last week, the system went silent.

The last alert before last week’s attacks was issued on September 29, for the southern province of Najran, according to posts on the civil defence X account.

The civil defences authority has continued to issue warnings about staying out of harm’s way during adverse weather, including rain and flooding, and did so as recently as Monday.

It also warned residents not to share images, rumours or information about interceptions and impact sites, including in a post on ​Monday, under government regulations issued in March.

Reuters could not determine whether anyone had faced prosecution for sharing such information, and the Saudi government media office did not respond to a request for comment on the matter.

Before last week’s airport attacks, officials from an allied Western ​government asked Saudi authorities why the alerts had stopped, two officials with direct knowledge of the matter said.

The response was that the alerts were too disruptive and many citizens had complained they were being woken by them at night, the officials said.

The Saudi government media office and Saudi officials ‌did not respond ⁠to requests for comment on the assertion.

Former US ambassador to Saudi Arabia Michael Ratney said Riyadh was trying to balance public messaging on attacks with efforts to prevent disruption in the kingdom but had ended up adding to a sense of unease about the strikes.

Riyadh airport to remain shut this week

“Their approach to public messaging seems like a corollary to the quandary they are in: They need to respond to the Houthis but don’t want that to result in societal disruption and their public messaging is a reflection of that,” he said.

“But the lack of alerts of incoming Houthi attacks creates the very nervousness they are trying to avoid.”

Ali Shihabi, a Saudi analyst close to the government, said that with or without early warnings, the kingdom would struggle to defend all of its assets because of its size.

“In Saudi Arabia you have ​too much to protect. It’s a huge country with airports, pipelines ​and oil facilities. There is just not enough coverage to ⁠defend everything at once, not enough Patriots (missile defence systems), interceptors and missile batteries to do it all,” he said.

“Saudi Arabia has an unlimited need for air defences,” he added.“

Despite the attacks, Saudi Arabia hosted an international conference on Monday, though major oil bosses dropped out.

At the World Petroleum Council Energy Congress in Riyadh,Saudi Prince Abdulaziz bin Salaman, a brother of the Saudi crown prince and the kingdom’s energy ​minister, struck a defiant tone while acknowledging risks and Saudi Arabia’s intent to keep its economic plans on track.

He thanked all who had travelled to Riyadh “because you know this country is safe” ​but added:

“Our gathering here does not ⁠mean the risk is gone.” “We will never forfeit any chance to maintain our commitment and our vision,” he said.

Embassies issue their own internal alerts

Despite no public alerts being issued this month until Monday, Riyadh has been attacked about a dozen times, two of the Western officials said.

During that time, Western embassies in the kingdom have been issuing their own internal missile and drone alerts to staff, according to three people familiar with the matter and alerts seen by Reuters.

These internal alerts are compiled from a mixture of US and other Western government intelligence and input from Saudi authorities, ⁠one of those ​people said.

They include alerts sent to staff around the time of two first airport strikes last week according to the people familiar with the matter.

They said that ​even the embassies had received no internal warning before Saturday’s airport strike, without offering an explanation.

One dead in new attack on Saudi airport, a day after Houthi strike kills 13

Reuters could not determine why no warning came before Saturday’s attack, the deadliest of last week’s attacks.

On Sunday, Saudi state TV released footage of Saturday’s strike.

It showed several shots of travellers in the airport terminal. Dozens lined up to board ​a flight. Men and women sat in chairs waiting, their eyes trained on the screens of their mobile phones as they scrolled.

Then, the bright orange flash of a missile explosion.

article_text:
Pakistan’s inflation rate is projected to rise to 9.9% in 2027, while economic growth is expected to ease to 3.5%, according to data released by the International Monetary Fund’s (IMF)World Economic Outlook (WEO)released on Tuesday.

The IMF data showed inflation at 7.1% in 2026, up from 4.5% in 2025. Pakistan’s gross domestic product (GDP) growth is projected at 3.6% in 2026, compared with 3.2% in 2025, before moderating to 3.5% in 2027.

According to theWEO, Pakistan’s current account balance is projected to remain flat in 2026 before slipping into a deficit equivalent to 1% of GDP in 2027, compared with a surplus of 0.5% of GDP in 2025.

Moreover, the country’s unemployment rate is forecast to decline to 6.9% in 2026 and 6.5% in 2027, from 7.1% in 2025, the data showed.

As per the report, global growth is projected to slow to 3.1% in 2026 and rebound to 3.4% in 2027. Global headline inflation is projected to rise notably to 4.7% in 2026 before easing to 4.1% in 2027.

The outlook noted that the global economy is again proving resilient, but unevenly so and with rapidly narrowing margins of adjustment in the near term.

“Activity in the first half of 2026 held up better than expected despite the dragging war in the Middle East and continuing strains from trade tensions.

“The technology cycle has provided a demand impulse, driven by strong investment in artificial intelligence (AI).

“The interaction of these forces—geopolitics and technology—has produced a split global economy: Favourable terms of trade or technology-related exports and investment give some countries a cushion, whereas others face higher import bills and weaker demand.

“Use of buffers and adaptability have helped economies weather the negative shocks so far. Flexible supply responses, rerouting of shipments, inventory drawdowns, fiscal support measures, and lower energy intensity than in previous decades have helped contain the hit to activity from the war.”

According to the outlook, energy-importing economies outside the technology value chain face the most difficult outlook. But the margins of adjustment that helped resilience are not limitless, and risks are skewed to the downside.

Further escalation in conflicts, a reassessment of expectations surrounding AI, renewed trade tensions, and fiscal vulnerabilities could weaken growth. On the upside, stronger momentum in AI investment and productivity gains from AI or a sustained easing of geopolitical and trade tensions could strengthen growth, read the report.

ISLAMABAD: Tax advisers, consultants, tax experts and chartered accountants have requested the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) chairman to further extend date by November 15, 2026 keeping in view genuine concerns.

In a communication to FBR Chairman on Monday, Javed Iqbal Qazi, Advocate Supreme Court and Chairman of the Pakistan Tax Advisers Association, requested for extension in time for filing of Income Tax returns/Wealth statements for the Tax Year 2026 which falls due on 15.10.2026.

Due to financial constraints/crises in country, very slow functioning of IRIS system, load-shedding problems being faced in different areas of the country and heavy burden on tax practitioners, advocates and chartered accountants the target fixed for number of returns cannot be achieved by October 15, 2026.

At present about 60-65 percent of the work has been completed by all tax practitioners and target fixed by the FBR will not be achieved by 15.10.2026.

The quantum of returns required to be filed by the taxpayers through the above noted three categories of the tax practitioners is too heavy and requires lot of time for the preparation of returns, as new columns have been inserted in the return forms which require lot of time for submission of the same, deposit of tax through CPRNS in the banks and submission on IRIS system.

The Pakistan Tax Advisers Association has received many massages from our members throughout the country to help the taxpayers/tax practitioners for the redressal of the genuine demand of the public at large and to achieve the financial targets fixed by FBR on the following grounds.

i) That manual return for low-income taxpayers has not been uploaded as yet on IRIS system.

ii) That the functioning of IRIS portal is very slow and takes too much time for uploading of the return which has been made too lengthy and tedious.

iii) That the financial position of the taxpayers have not allowed them to deposit their tax liability in the government exchequer in time.

Javed Iqbal Qazi has requested the FBR chairman that in the interest of justice and fair play, it is prayed that the taxpayers, the tax practitioners be facilitated and the last date of submission of returns be extended upto November 15, 2026.

The FBR proposes expanding income tax rules from YouTube to all social media platforms by amending existing provisions, aiming to broaden the digital tax framework for online content creators.

ISLAMABAD: The Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) has proposed expanding the scope of income tax rules from YouTube to all social media platforms, potentially bringing a wider range of online content creators and digital platforms within the existing tax framework.

The FBR has drafted notifications proposing amendments to the Income Tax Rules, 2002, replacing the word “YouTube” with “social media platforms” in two separate provisions dealing with income tax.

Under the first proposed amendment, the FBR seeks to revise clause (d) of sub-rule (1) of rule 13ZP in Chapter IIA of the Income Tax Rules, 2002. The amendment is being proposed under section 99C, read with sub-section (1) of section 237 of the Income Tax Ordinance, 2001.

The second draft notification proposes a similar change in clause (d) of sub-rule (1) of rule 19R in Chapter VA of the Income Tax Rules, 2002. This amendment is proposed under section 99C, read with clause (b) of sub-section (3B) of section 101 and sub-section (1) of section 237 of the Income Tax Ordinance, 2001.

By replacing the platform-specific reference to YouTube with the broader term “social media platforms”, the proposed changes could extend the relevant provisions beyond YouTube to other social media services.

The FBR has invited objections and suggestions from all persons likely to be affected by the proposed amendments. Stakeholders have been given seven days from publication of the draft notifications in the official Gazette to submit their feedback for consideration by the Board.

The notifications state that objections and suggestions received within the prescribed period will be considered by the FBR before proceeding further.

The proposed amendments remain at the draft stage and do not, by themselves, establish that the changes have been finalised or brought into force.

Pakistan expects to achieve its electric vehicle adoption targets ahead of schedule, primarily due to surging oil prices making EVs more economically attractive for consumers.

Amid the growing popularity of electric vehicles (EVs), Pakistan expects to reach its EV adoption target ahead of schedule as consumers increasingly switch from petrol- or diesel-powered cars.

“I feel that the target we had set in our electric-vehicle policy last year, we will achieve it much earlier as the rise in oil prices has brought cost recovery of EVs to one to one-and-a-half year,” Haroon Akhtar, adviser to the prime minister on industries and production, toldBloomberg.

Pakistan has developed policies to promote the adoption of Electric Vehicles (EVs) to reduce its fuel import bill, improve environmental conditions, and foster a sustainable transport system.

In 2019, the government approved the National Electric Vehicles Policy (NEVP) in 2019. The initial goals included EVs making up 30% of all passenger vehicle and heavy-duty truck sales by 2030, and 90% by 2040.

Since the Middle East war started in February, petrol and diesel prices have jumped 54% and 43%, respectively, according to Pakistan State Oil Company Ltd. This has shortened the time it takes for buyers to recoup the higher upfront cost of an EV, Akhtar toldBloomberg.

Oil prices climbed on Thursdayon persistent worries about supply from the key Middle East producing region amid an increase in attacks on shipping in the Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz, while the US cut output as a hurricane menaced offshore production.

Brent crude futures rose $2.28, or 2.28%, to $102.28 a barrel by 0427 GMT. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures gained $1.66, or 1.88%, to $89.94.

Meanwhile, the official toldBloombergthat the government is also preparing a new auto policy that could be presented to the cabinet within the next two weeks. The government is considering tax incentives for EVs to narrow their price gap with conventional vehicles, Akhtar said.

Last year, theNational Electric Vehicle (NEV) Policy 2025-30was officially launched in June 2025, after being finalised in November 2024 and approved by the Economic Coordination Committee in October 2025.

article_text:
MILAN: US builder Caddell Construction has formally committed to pay €30.941 ​million ($35.24 million) in a probe into alleged worker exploitation at the site of the new US consulate ‌in Milan, a document seen byReutersshowed.

The Alabama-based construction giant undertook to pay nearly €20 million to workers in overtime, accommodation reimbursements and compensation for non-material damages, according to a document submitted by the firm to Milan prosecutors. It did not admit any liability.

Caddell did not respond to ​a request for comment.

In a statement issued in June, Caddell said it was proactively cooperating with judicial authorities and ​was “committed to treating and paying workers fairly”.

The company specialises in large-scale projects, including contracts for US ⁠embassies and military facilities.

Caddell Construction’s Italian unit was placed under investigation for alleged labour exploitation and put under judicial administration on ​May 29, a measure upheld by a judge two weeks later.

Milan prosecutors and Italy’s Carabinieri police accused the company of recruiting workers ​in India through an intermediary based in New Delhi and employing them on “exhausting shifts, underpaid, without safety protections and under the constant threat of dismissal”.

Iran insists on diplomatic solution after Trump rejects peace plan

The company has also agreed to pay more than €7 million to Italy’s social security agency INPS and almost €4 million to the Labour Inspectorate, the ​document showed.

In the letter to Milan prosecutors, signed by Caddell Construction executive officer Michael Angelo Ranieri and reviewed by Reuters, the ​US company stressed that its commitments did not amount to any admission of wrongdoing.

“Furthermore, they do not imply any acceptance of the legal ‌and factual ⁠assessments made by the authorities involved,” it added.

Case against company set to be dismissed after payment

Two sources with direct knowledge of the matter said the agreement involves the regularisation of around 500 workers, the recognition by the Italian state of residence permits for 270 foreign workers and unemployment benefits for 60 workers who had been dismissed.

One of the two sources said that, once ​the payments had been made, ​Milan prosecutors were expected to ⁠seek the dismissal of the case against Caddell’s Italian unit.

The source added that prosecutors were expected to pursue plea bargain agreements with two Caddell executives arrested as part of the investigation.

Construction ​on the US consulate in Milan started in 2022. The contract was worth almost $210 million ​and work was ⁠initially scheduled to finish in 2025, but this date was subsequently put back to 2028.

A US State Department spokesperson told Reuters in June that US law enforcement was cooperating with the Italian authorities, and that “the US government does not tolerate labour exploitation”.

This is the ⁠latest in ​a series of labour exploitation investigations conducted in recent years by Milan prosecutor Paolo ​Storari.

The probes have forced companies to grant fuller employment rights to more than 60,000 workers and enabled authorities to recover more than €1 billion ($1.1 billion), while also ​fuelling a heated debate over whether Italy’s judiciary is overstepping its role.

article_text:
The Federal Reserve, under new chief Kevin Warsh, raised interest rates to combat persistent inflation driven by tariffs, energy costs, and AI spending, with further hikes anticipated.

WASHINGTON: The Federal Reserve raised interest rates on Wednesday and flagged further increases in borrowing costs in coming months, with new US central bank chief Kevin Warsh joining a unanimous decision that effectively acknowledges the Trump administration’s inability so far to control inflation.

While President Donald Trump had promised to lower prices on his watch, the combined impact of his global import tariffs, an energy shock following the start of the US-Israeli war with Iran, and capital spending from the artificial intelligence boom has kept price pressures intense enough that the Fed felt it needed to raise its benchmark overnight interest rate by a quarter of a percentage point to the 3.75%-4.00% range.

New policy projections showed 16 of 18 policymakers anticipate at least one more quarter-percentage-point hike by the end of this year, with only two of them seeing rates remaining stable from here. Warsh apparently again did not submit a rate projection.

It’s the first policy shift under the new Fed chief, who took office in late May after being selected by Trump with an expectation that he would cut rates.

Also read:Fed holds rates steady; three policymakers dissent in favor of a hike

The Fed’s new policy statement and economic projections, to the contrary, show a central bank opening the door on tighter monetary policy through next year, with the policy rate rising to the 4.00%-4.25% range by the end of this year and ending 2027 at the same level.

“Today’s policy action will support a timelier return to the Committee’s 2% goal,” the central bank said in its policy statement after the end of a two-day meeting.

While the statement withheld any forward guidance about coming policy decisions, as is Warsh’s preference, the decision is likely to ease doubts that the Fed chief would hold off on tighter policy out of deference to Trump, a lingering question during his first months in office.

The statement dropped a previous reference attributing current elevated inflation to “supply shocks” particularly in the energy sector, a nod to concerns among policymakers, including Warsh, that price pressures were too broad for comfort.

Warsh is scheduled to hold a press conference beginning at 2:30 p.m. EDT (1830 GMT) to elaborate on the decision.

The rate increase was announced less than two months ahead of midterm elections that will determine whether Trump’s Republicans maintain control of Congress for the final two years of his presidency.

The Republicans are facing an uphill battle with voters angry about gasoline prices that are about a third higher than a year ago and interest rates on home mortgages that have been rising steadily this year. The average rate on a 30-year fixed-rate mortgage is approaching 7%.

Policymakers’ new quarterly economic projections marked up estimates of inflation, as measured by the Personal Consumption Expenditures Price Index, to 3.7% versus the 3.6% projected at the Fed’s June meeting. Inflation is not projected to return to the 2% target until 2029, a year later than previously expected.

Economic growth was marked up slightly from 2.2% to 2.3%, while the unemployment rate is seen ending the year at 4.1%, versus the 4.3% projected in June.

Warsh’s characterization at his press conference of the logic behind the rate increase and the likelihood of further action will be important in shaping the reaction in financial markets that have been raising yields on long-term US Treasury bonds.

The rate hike on Wednesday was widely expected, but investors will be looking for further information from the Fed chief about what might prompt additional increases in borrowing costs.

Warsh has pledged to lower inflation back to 2% “clearly and at sufficient speed” by raising rates as needed.
